paper_title: On the Stability of Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching on the Line
classifications: Theory of computation → Design and analysis of algorithms
statement: We studied the stability of online algorithms for the minimum-weight perfect matching √ problem in R1 . We presented an O( n)-stable algorithm with approximation ratio 2, which we showed to be optimal among any algorithm with sublinear stability. We conjecture that √ Ω( n) is necessary to achieve approximation ratio 2. We also proved that any algorithm with o(log n) stability must have an unbounded approximation ratio. It would be interesting to see what approximation ratio can be achieved with an f (n)-stable algorithm for f (n) in the range √ from Θ(log n) to Θ( n). We conjecture that it is possible, for any integer constant α > 1, to deterministically maintain a (2α − 1)-approximation with an O(n1/α )-stable algorithm similar to what Goranci et al. [6] achieve using randomization in the bipartite setting.
